newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories up in May as sales weaken.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories up in May as sales weaken.

text.p: Inventories held by businesses rose moderately in May as sales dropped at the sharpest rate in nearly a year, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday.

Total business inventories rose 0.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted $1.02 trillion after a revised 0.4 percent gain in April, the department said. Previously the department said inventories had risen only 0.3 percent in April.
Unsold stocks of goods, including furniture, food and building materials, mounted at retail stores in May, though inventories were drawn down at new-car dealers and at general merchandise stores.
Wall Street economists had forecast a slightly higher increase of 0.3 percent in overall May inventories.

The report was consistent with other signs that economic growth moderated sharply in the second quarter from the first quarter's sizzling 5.9 percent annual rate of expansion, largely because consumers reined in spending.

Total sales by all types of businesses declined in May by 0.5 percent from April to $743.2 billion after a 0.2 percent pickup in April. Department officials said it was the largest drop in monthly sales since a 0.7 percent fall in June last year.

Sales at manufacturing companies dropped 1 percent to $323.5 billion in May following a 1.2 percent April increase. At retailers they dropped for a second month in a row, down 0.3 percent in May to $209.3 billion after a 1.1 percent plunge in April.
Only wholesalers reported a small May increase in sales, up 0.2 percent to $210.4 billion following a 0.1 percent drop in April.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to deplete existing stocks at the current sales pace -- rose to 1.37 months' worth in May from 1.36 months in April.
